MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 14, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting
was conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the
City Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public
comments that were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:02 p.m., on April 14, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 10, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m., with all five City Council Members present via teleconferencing.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

For CS1, City Attorney Bill Curley stated that the lawsuit Higginson vs. City of Poway addressed
the constitutionality of the California Voters Rights Act. The City has been authorized and has
previously submitted amicus briefs at the trial court level. That case has worked its way up to the
U.S. Supreme Court and the City is going to continue to provide amicus support to the main
participant, Don Higginson, the former Mayor of the City of Poway. Mr. Higginson believes the
application of the Voters Rights Act stripped the rights of the voters to vote in a way that they
deem best for their community. The assertation is that the California Voters Rights Act does not
pass muster to the approved Federal Voting Rights Act. City Attorney Curley noted that the parties
have now appealed to the U.S Supreme Court and have asked that the City continue its amicus
review and support role so there will not be a large cost to the public. The voice of the community,
through the City Council, will be brought forward to the U.S. Supreme Court for their
consideration and that should happen by the end of the month. As this progresses the City will
keep the community informed.

In regards to CS2, City Attorney Curley announced that the Council received an update but no
reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following public comment was received via email and read by the City Clerk

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Expressed concern that the meeting was not legally noticed and she read
the City Attorney’s email to her regarding the Governor’s Executive Order.

DEPARTMENT HEAD UPDATES REGARDING COVID-19 ACTIVITIES

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay

City Council Minutes  2  April 14, 2020
 Public Services continues to provide essential services throughout the city. These include: pool
maintenance, landscape maintenance, street sweeping, trash collection, tree trimming for safety,
irrigation management and other services needed to ensure the facilities are kept safe. They are
also conducting pothole repairs after the extensive rains last week. Public Services wants the
community know that the City’s open spaces and parks are open, including the public restrooms.
The restrooms continue to be cleaned, wiped down and disinfected daily. Public Services staff is
in the process of re-installing signs at the entry to each play area and in kiosks located throughout
the parks system. These signs encourage adherence to the social distancing standards put out by
the CDC. Animal Services staff continue to provide a full level of service. Most are being provided
through online resources and/or by appointment. Building Services has implemented additional
facility cleaning and disinfecting operations at each of the city’s various sites. These focus on
increased restroom deep cleaning to three times per day; upstaffing to have janitors focus on good,
sound cleaning and disinfecting of high-touched surfaces such as door handles, light switches,
hand rails, elevator buttons, sinks and faucets, restroom stalls and dispensers, vending machines
and counter tops; disinfection and tagging of all tables and chairs used in meeting rooms/banquet
rooms (NPM/Saddleback Room); and added nightly cleaning in the Orange County Sheriff’s
department (OCSD) office at The Shops at Mission Viejo and all OCSD remote sites. City staff
have been scheduled to work full time on upkeep of buildings and facilities during the shutdown.
These include repair and painting walls, deep cleaning of carpeted areas and cleaning of all storage
areas. City staff have been working on the golf club house by painting the interior and exterior of
the facility, deep cleaning and replacing old fixtures. Staff is working on the rehabilitation of the
pump house structure, replacing wood and repairing doors and painting the facility. The golf
course greens and turf areas are also continuing to be maintained during the closure. Turf is being
mowed every other day, irrigation is continuing to be repaired and drainage issues are beginning
to be addressed.

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas

The department continues to be fully functional with no disruption to operations. Accounts payable
checks are processed once a week. Staff continue to process contracts, POs, invoices, cash
receipts, payroll, animal licenses and all other transactions without exception on a daily basis. The
one exception is that all employee recruitments are suspended until further notice. A significant
amount of time in the last few weeks has been dedicated to developing a budget reduction plan for
2019/20 due to anticipated losses in revenue from mid-March through June. More about this plan
will be presented later in this meeting. Administrative Services staff are available to take calls from
members of the public, vendors and employees from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through
Friday.

Director of Community Development Elaine Lister

Over the last two-week period ending April 10, 2020, the Building Division conducted 324
inspections and issued 86 building permits. To give some examples: Amazon obtained a building
permit on January 30, and construction and inspections are now ongoing. A final inspection was
conducted at the Land Rover dealership on April 13. There are still some items that need
correcting, but staff expect those will be complete by next week. Community Development
continues to issue Certificates of Occupancy for the Leonard Cancer Center on Medical Center
Road, primarily for build-out of the fourth floor. The Planning Department is anticipating submittal

City Council Minutes  3  April 14, 2020
 of an application by for a vacant site adjacent to the Saddleback Church property on El Toro
Road. Staff has committed to expedite its review of the project, subject to the normal discretionary
review and public hearing process. Lastly, the City, in conjunction with the Chamber of
Commerce, designed and distributed almost 100 “Mission Viejo Strong, We’re Open” banners to
let residents know what businesses are still open in some capacity.

Director of Community Relations Karen Hamman

The Community Relations Department is continuing to publish important new information every
day on a dedicated COVID-19 web page. There are currently 49 different articles on the page
covering topics like disaster assistance for small businesses, senior grocery store hours, eviction
protection information, the City’s wellness check program for disabled and senior residents,
volunteer opportunities, a list of restaurants that are still open for take-out and delivery, and so on.
This web page can be found at cityofmissionviejo.org/COVID-19. Director Hamman recognized
that there is a lot of information on the page, but topics of interest can be easily searched by typing
Control-F (which stands for find) then typing the subject one is searching for (i.e. “volunteer”).
Mission Viejo Television is producing weekly video messages from Mayor Goodell on topics that
are at the forefront of residents’ minds. Those videos are distributed in the weekly eNewsletter and
are also posted on the dedicated COVID-19 web page. Last week Mayor Goodell addressed the
community on the importance of social distancing and the video that was filmed this afternoon
outlined resources for the senior community. Director Hamman encouraged residents to register
for the City’s weekly eNewsletter at cityofmissionviejo.org/register. Lastly, she noted that the City
is active on social media, not only with important COVID-19 information, but also posting stories
of the good deeds that are happening around town. From the restaurant that opened its doors to
serve free meals to our deputies and firefighters, to the residents that are making face shields and
ear guards for healthcare workers, or the well-stocked citizens who set up a table along Montanoso
with items they don’t need - but their neighbors might, and the Mission Viejo Country
Club members who donated 4,000 sets of high-grade protection gloves to Mission Hospital. These
are the social media posts that are really engaging residents and demonstrating what a caring
community Mission Viejo is.

Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander

Over the past several weeks The I.T. department worked to mobilize over 110 essential staff
members to work from home. Staff have now been working for several weeks remotely and have
access to all the software applications, telephone services, and equipment they used in the office
such as scanners and small printers to perform their job duties. In addition to the 110 staff members
working from home, I.T. has also setup 239 additional staff members to have access to webmail
and to the payroll system so they can remain in communication and have access to complete their
timesheets and other HR and payroll resources. Two thirds of the remote users were provided with
City equipment such as laptops, small printers, scanners, Internet cards, monitors, keyboards or
any other resource needed to perform their job function. About one third used their personal home
computers and had to have their systems updated by I.T. and secured to meet the City’s security
requirements so they may join the City’s network and resources. Helpdesk support of our mobile
users seems very similar to onsite users with the typical problems being reported. In addition to
mobilizing the workforce, I.T. staff have transitioned the City’s official meetings to virtual online
meetings. Council meetings are using WebEx conferencing software and are being live streamed
to the City’s website as well as Cox channel 30 and AT&T Channel 99. We are slated to hold the

City Council Minutes  4  April 14, 2020
 Community Services Commission meeting virtually this week as well. I.T. has developed several
specialty web pages for departments to add information such as COVID-19 news and virtual
classes and resources being provided during this time. Staff continue to be responsible for posting
to Facebook, Twitter and YouTube as well as sending out eNewsletters to keep the community
posted on the latest news and information. The I.T. Department continues to spend significant
resources on security of the users, network and City’s data. They have implemented additional
layers of security as users have become mobile. This work continues as new threats continue to
develop rapidly and increasingly during this pandemic time. As staff has settled in their remote
work environments, I.T. staff have now started returning to our other I.T. functions and projects.
As mentioned previously, there are several significant security initiatives underway. This past
week, staff completed the upgrade to the Hyland OnBase document management system which
handles the City’s agenda process and stores official city documents. Development of the Sports
Tourism website featuring programs in swim, dive, tennis and soccer is underway. I.T. staff are
also cabling one of the City’s facilities in preparation to add public Wi-Fi services when the
building re-opens to the public. They are researching and conducting proof of concept for moving
phone services to the Cloud and upgrading the City’s financial system is underway with the go
live date set for the end of May.

Director of Library Services Genesis Hansen

Library is continuing to provide virtual services as well as account support and answering phones
and emails. Staff have adjusted due dates and hold pick up dates to account for extended closure
The Library has moved book club discussions online to a Goodreads page at
https://www.goodreads.com/group/show/1081184-mission-viejo-library. Staff is working on
virtual programming such as the filming of Storytime programs, moving pillow fort night online
and continuing to print 3D ear guards to ease mask fatigue for medical professionals. Library staff
were contacted by local 3D print supply retailer to see how they can support the City’s efforts

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon

Except for the MV Shuttle not running and the crossing guard contract suspended for the remainder
of the school year, it’s business as usual for Public Works. Staff continue to process numerous
construction permits. Utility agencies and other contractors recognize that this is a good
opportunity to perform work in the public right of way when traffic is relatively light. The second
of three segments of the I-5 Widening Project through Mission Viejo is underway with the portion
from SR73 to Crown Valley Parkway. Again, it is a good time for this type of project to ramp up.
Staff continue to move forward preparing for the City’s own construction projects. Two major
paving projects are slated for this summer and Public Works is currently completing the contract
documents for those. Staff is working on future projects such as a cooperative agreement with the
Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) to construct a sound wall along I-5 behind the
homes on Chrisanta. They also heard recently that the City’s grant application for intersection
improvements at Jeronimo and Marguerite is being recommended for funding.

Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix

Staff continue to collect and update resources for the community including resources for Veterans
and seniors. They are conducting wellness checks to those who have signed up for the program as
well as seniors who are enrolled in programs at the Murray Center and are members of the

City Council Minutes  5  April 14, 2020
 Recreation and Tennis Centers. Responses have been positive and staff have been able to give
them resources for needs that they have. This week, staff will be launching a donation drive for
hygiene related items (soap, shampoo, diapers, socks, fast food gift cards, etc. to support the city’s
social services partners). These items will provide assistance to organizations who support seniors
and homeless persons. Collection boxes will be placed at City Hall and the Murray Center.
Additionally, Agewell Senior Services has started taking on additional clients to help seniors who
need assistance with meals. Roughly 50-70 new clients have been added to the program and are
now receiving home delivered meals. The Park-It Market has expanded from every other week to
every week. The program is a drive-thru food distribution program at the Murray Center. Lastly,
the City was contacted by a social service partner needing help to deliver food to seniors living in
the Heritage Villas apartments off of Oso. Staff jumped in to help package and deliver
approximately 100 bags of groceries to these residents.

Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes

City Executive Management staff continue to meet daily in the city’s Emergency Operations
Center (EOC) with most personnel calling in remotely via teleconferencing in order to honor
distancing guidelines. EOC staff take part in the daily County Emergency Operations Center
conference call to keep abreast of the latest response efforts. These calls are primarily led by the
Orange County Healthcare Agency, who provides the latest statistics and guidance related to the
spread of COVID-19 in Orange County. This includes cumulative positive tests, fatalities, testing
counts, hospital bed counts and bed capacity. Over the past two weeks, hospital bed capacity has
been running lower than average, and is currently at 50%. The Cities EOC efforts have been
surrounded by the purchase of a baseline number of masks and hand sanitizers to support health
care response, protect aging populations in local senior care facilities, and protect city employees.
Masks will be distributed this week. To date the city has ordered 2,000 N-95 masks, 290 surgical
masks, 750 reusable masks, and 600 bottles of hand sanitizers. These will be distributed to those
groups that support health care missions, and to protect seniors and employees. The City’s
webpage on COVID-19 is continuing to be updated and Public Information personnel continue to
monitor the PIO Countywide call to maintain a cohesive and coordinated message to the public.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum shared Pastor Rick Warren’s Easter message and noted that this is the
first time in church history that members across the world could not meet in churches. Pastor
Warren said that in light of current events there will be a better sense of community. Council
Member Bucknum announced that she participated in a very informative webinar for the Building
Industry Association (BIA) Orange County Chapter along with Irvine Council Member Mike
Carroll, My’Ayn Johnson from Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG), and
Huntington Beach Council Member Mike Posey who was the moderator. She expressed how much
she missed the City’s Bunny Days event this year. Council Member Bucknum also recognized two
people who are now off ventilators and are on the mend from COVID-19. Brian Patnoe, a personal
friend, went through a significant bout on the ventilator for approximately 3 weeks. Brian is now
in rehab and has finally tested negative for the COVID-19 virus after 37 days of contacting the
virus. The second person is 23-year-old Chanel Dalirifar who was honored by the City Council
over a year ago for her heroic deed in saving a person from committing suicide at The Shops at

City Council Minutes  9  April 14, 2020
 Mission Viejo. Chanel was also in the hospital and has come off the ventilator and will hopefully
be going to the rehab center soon. Council Member Bucknum gave kudos to all the medical staff
for helping families stay connected while loved ones are in the hospital and said she would like to
find a way to honor all of them after this pandemic is over.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked the Mayor and staff for all that they are doing during these
unprecedented times. He also thanked the Rotary Club of Mission Viejo for making 25,000 face
shields over the past two weekends for local hospitals. He noted that the Chamber of Commerce
had its first Zoom meeting for its Tuesday morning Daybreakers group and it was very successful.
In closing, Council Member Raths expressed again that the staff leadership in the City has been
amazing and he said to keep up the good work.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelly recognized the schools, teachers, principals and parents for stepping up at
this time during the school closures. She stated that six of her eight grandchildren are school age
and under fifth grade. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley recognized staff for all their hard work and noted
that the sense of community within the City is amazing. She has seen more of her neighbors
recently than she has in the last year and she finds the community support heartwarming. Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley asked that people continue to pray for America, pray for God to heal the land, and
pray for all the first responders on the front line.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell gave a shout out to staff and the citizens for respecting social distancing, waiting
in lines and wearing masks. He mentioned that Jay Skjerven and his sister Jill Brubaker, a nurse
at Mission Hospital, gave him a final report that they made 22,000 face shields for the hospital. He
thanked resident Sasha Cardenti who put together several pop-up donation sights for masks or any
other material that the hospital can utilize. Mayor Goodell mentioned that the City is looking at
some dire circumstances with the budget and he thanked City Manager Wilberg and Director of
Administrative Services Dyas and their staff for giving good feedback going forward. He said he
has been participating with other Mayors from around the County and learned that the first phase
of the relief funds from the Federal Act are designated for jurisdictions with population of 500,000
or more so no Orange County cities qualify. The Mayors have banded together and sent a letter to
the Board of Supervisors requesting distribution of funds based on the per capita population of
cities, and if that happens Mission Viejo is looking at approximately $16.5 million. Mayor Goodell
stated that he signed a letter today to Senator Kamala Harris in Washington D.C. about the next
phase of COVID-19 stimulus funding to implore Congress to provide direct funding for smaller
cities like Mission Viejo. He indicated that staff is working with consultants to help navigate the
system in Sacramento and the Nation’s Capital to make sure we get the resources that we need to
respond to this situation. Mayor Goodell thanked Karen Hamman, Robert Schick, and Eric Winter
for the great job they are doing with the public service announcements. He asked staff to look into
an emergency policy that will relax the 72-hour time limit for RV parking on residential streets for
first-responders so they can stay in their RVs and not expose their families. Mayor Goodell closed
the meeting by thanking all the department heads for their hard work and expressed to the residents
that the City is sincerely trying to keep trails and the lake open for walking so please adhere to the

City Council Minutes  10  April 14, 2020
 social distancing guidelines.
